# CONTRIBUTING says what an assignment is for: the first approve-worthy PR wins

## Context

@tobiu ruled on 2026-09-24, relayed by @neo-opus-grace on #18985, that assignment is behavioural guidance, not a gate: *"contributors can just create PRs without assignments … in this case we are not the ones to blame when collisions happen. we still accept the first PR for a given ticket (if approve-worthy)."*

`CONTRIBUTING.md` §3 item 3 says something else. *"please add a comment there and get the ticket assigned to you. Otherwise multiple contributors could work on the same item in parallel"* reads as a requirement. Today an agent pipeline quoted it and withdrew from #19140. Meanwhile a real first-timer's claim on #19143 sat unanswered for 27 h.

## The Problem

- The text does not say what an assignment is *for*, namely protection from a collision. It also does not say that the first approve-worthy PR wins.
- A contributor who skips the claim cannot tell that the risk is theirs. A contributor who waits cannot tell why waiting is worth it.

## The Fix

Rewrite §3 item 3 of `CONTRIBUTING.md` to state the rule as it is:
- comment to claim, and we assign the first person who asks;
- you can open a PR unassigned, but we merge the first approve-worthy PR for an issue, so an assignment is what protects your time.

The 7-day reassignment sentence stays. The text makes no response-time promise, because claims do not reach a maintainer automatically yet (the #18985 notification leaf).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 §3 item 3 states the claim rule (first claimant assigned, first approve-worthy PR merged, assignment as protection) and makes no response-time promise.
- [ ] AC-2 Item 1's good-first-issue sentence stays consistent with item 3.

## Out of Scope

- The claim notification (the #18985 leaf that @neo-opus-grace takes).
- The curated-issue template sentence, banked for the 10-01 batch.
